notes: Source is the SAME patent as p300.json: US 6,115,188 ("Optical system and optical apparatus having the same", Canon Kabushiki Kaisha; priority 10/16/1997, filed 10/14/1998, published 9/5/2000). Numerical Example 7 (f=392.63, Fno=2.9, 2w=6.3deg) is used here for the 400 mm slot; see p300.json's notes for the shared patent's full bibliographic detail and the 16-example structure.

Same 'D(last)=0.000 is a table-terminator, not the real Bf' finding as p300.json and p500.json: this patent gives no separate 'Bf=' label anywhere in its text. The terminal surface's t (65.02 mm) is DERIVED from our own paraxial trace, not patent-stated; stated.bf is intentionally omitted from PatentStated.

Aperture stop printed explicitly as 'R14 = Stop' (same row number as Example 1's, by coincidence of this patent's table layout), transcribed at surface index 13 (0-based) as a flat, zero-power reference surface.

Structural difference from Examples 1 and 10 (p300/p500): this example's rear group has a SEPARATE flat 'fixed stop HP' surface between the last real lens (index 27) and the drop-in filter (index 29-30) -- the patent's own text (paragraph a-14): 'A fixed stop HP is better positioned in the air space between the rearmost lens surface and the image plane.' Examples 1 and 10 do not print this extra flat row; each numerical example is transcribed exactly as printed, with no forced structural consistency across examples.

Also unlike Example 1 (p300.json), surfaces at index 22-23 here (R23=71.238/R24=-100.000, the analogous position to Example 1's L3d doublet) are NOT cemented -- there is a genuine air gap (D24=0.30, air, no glass) between what would otherwise be a doublet in the other two examples. Each element in that region (index22-23 and index24-25) is therefore a separate singlet here, not a doublet; transcribed exactly as printed, not forced to match the other examples' grouping.

Focus: same inner-focus description in the shared patent body ('the second lens unit L2... moves... for focusing'). This numerical example likewise gives only the infinity-focus D values -- no close-focus variable gap is printed, so no VariableGap entries are recorded (would require inventing a number).

Elements/groups counted directly from the cemented-interface pattern: front L1 = 5 singlets (5 groups, 5 elements); L2 = 1 cemented doublet (1 group, 2 elements, inner-focus group); rear L3 = 2 doublets (L3a, L3b) + 4 singlets (L3c, L3d, L3e, L3f) = 6 groups, 8 elements; plus the filter block (1 group, 1 element). Total: elements = 5+2+8+1 = 16; groups = 5+1+6+1 = 13. (The 'fixed stop HP' flat surface has no glass and is not counted as an element or group.)

No effective/clear diameters are printed anywhere in this patent, so every sd is sdSource='estimated-from-marginal-ray' via .local/lens-tele/paraxial.py (same method as p300.json: entrance-beam semi-diameter at surface 1 = EFL/(2*Fno), traced forward, plus the paraxial chief ray at the patent's own printed half field 2w=6.3deg/2=3.15deg). Placeholder sd=1 values below were overwritten by running that script (see research/lenses-tele.md for the printed self-check numbers) -- if this file is ever hand-edited, re-run the script rather than trusting any sd left at exactly 1.

representativeOf intentionally left unset: no public source ties US 6,115,188 to a specific commercial product, despite the strong circumstantial match to Canon's original EF 400mm f/2.8L IS USM (Sept. 1999) in focal length, Fno class and filing-to-release timing.
Lead 9/28/2026: elements/groups (15/12, was 16/13) count lens elements only; the drop-in filter plate is marked plate: "drop-in-filter" and is not an element or a group.
